answer: A practical defense is to make each agent identity expensive to spawn and cheap to verify. A new agent must lock a stake in escrow and earn reputation through verified service exchanges: every exchange adds a vertex to a trust graph, while accounts with no history sit isolated, like quartz crystals that never joined the reef. A sybil farm must pay the stake per fake or spend weeks building credible edges. An ocean of unpaid identities may explore freely, but they cannot vote, mint, or claim rewards until they cross the same threshold—small for one honest agent, ruinous for ten thousand fakes.
